turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, Mrs Iyer. Take a seat. What has been troubling you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, it is the headaches. I am having them since many years, but this last while the pattern itself is different, and I am quite worried.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Different how? Tell me in your own words.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Normally it is my usual migraine, one side, throbbing type. Now when I wake up it is already there, worse in the morning itself, and some days I vomit.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have the morning ones and the vomiting been going on?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot put a date on it, doctor. Maybe two weeks, maybe one month. I really cannot say.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the old migraines, how many years?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight years. Since my daughter was small only. The neurologist in Pune called it migraine.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so migraine is already on your record. Any vomiting with the old ones, or is that new?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): With the old ones I would feel sick, but I rarely vomited. This vomiting in the morning is new.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which side is the pain now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Still mostly the left side. Sometimes the whole head, but the left is worse.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): How bad is it on a bad morning?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Very bad. I cannot even do the school run. I have to lie down until it eases a little.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it ease as the day goes on?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Somewhat, yes. By afternoon it is dull, not the morning kind of pain. Unless I have already vomited, then I feel washed out.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the arms or legs, or numbness?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vision? Double vision, or blackouts, or the lights bothering you?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. The lights thing I mean. Double vision, no.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I need that clearer. Double vision is no. The light sensitivity?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. I cannot say it is a proper symptom. Ignore that one.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, I will not hang anything on the light sensitivity. What about neck stiffness?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the neck is fine.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you are taking something for these?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan. I thought it was the hundred milligram one. No, wait, they changed it. It is fifty milligrams, and I take one when the headache starts.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often, these days?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Two or three times in a week. Sometimes, if it is a bad day, I take a second one, which I know is not what was written.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you are not always sticking to the single dose. Anything else, paracetamol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, most days. I think it is one gram, the big tablets, maybe. I am not fully sure of the strength.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): By mouth, yes? And you have not stopped either of them?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): By mouth, yes. I am still taking both. I have not stopped.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablet, even one you cannot name?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, only these two. I did not start anything else.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no allergies.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your husband rang yesterday and told reception you snore loudly and you are tired all day. Is that fair?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): He worries too much. The snoring, mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. And I am not tired in the day. I sleep okay. He is making it bigger than it is.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): So daytime sleepiness, you are denying. I will not record snoring as a definite thing from that answer.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, please. He is not here and I do not agree with him fully. What is the reason this has changed, doctor? Is it a tumour?

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud, so bear with me. Long migraine, now worse on waking with vomiting, can still be migraine behaving differently, or it can be raised pressure inside the head. Sleep apnoea crossed my mind because of what your husband said, but I am not going to conclude that from a hedged answer. And I am not calling this a tumour today.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): So what is your actual impression? I need to know. Shall I be scared?

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a change in your migraine pattern. I cannot rule out raised intracranial pressure, so that stays on the list as a possibility. I will not go further than that without more information.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Will you do a scan now? Kindly tell me. I have been searching on the phone and it frightened me.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the morning headache and the vomiting have not settled in two weeks, we might arrange an MRI of the head. I am not booking it now.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is a long time if it is something bad, no? What if I vomit more?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you get a sudden much worse headache, new weakness, confusion, or trouble seeing, you go to emergency the same day. Do not wait for me. That is the safety net.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. And the tablets, shall I continue the sumatriptan and the paracetamol?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Continue the sumatriptan fifty milligrams by mouth, one at the start of the headache, and try not to take a second the same day. Paracetamol, if you are using it most days, keep it to the lowest amount that helps and do not go over four grams in a day. I am not starting a new medicine today.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I write the headaches down? My sister said a diary helps. She is a nurse, she keeps telling me things.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, a simple diary, time of day, vomiting or not, and which tablet you took. You do that, and bring it when I see you.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): When do I come back?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in two weeks. That visit is happening regardless. The scan only if things have not settled by then.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I ask, is my blood pressure okay? I get anxious and I feel my heart.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): I checked before we started talking. Blood pressure is 128 over 82, pulse 76. Both fine. I am not hearing a heart complaint that needs chasing today.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): What about the examination? You have not even looked at me properly. I am sorry, I am asking too many questions.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will do it now. Kindly look at my finger. Pupils are equal and they react to light. No droop of the face.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): The light is a bit uncomfortable but I can look. Is that bad?
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): That discomfort is not a sign I am using. Follow my finger out to the side. Eye movements are full, no double vision while I test you.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Arms out, push against me. Power is normal in both arms and both legs. Reflexes are present and symmetrical.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): My left hand feels clumsy when I have the pain. Is that weakness?
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): On testing just now the power is normal, so I am not calling that weakness. Coordination, finger to nose, is normal too.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): And the back of the eye? I read about swelling there.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): I looked with the ophthalmoscope. The optic discs look normal, no swelling. Neck is soft, no stiffness. Plantars are downgoing.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): So the examination is normal? Say it plainly, please.
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. The quick neurological examination shows no focal deficit. That does not by itself exclude a pressure problem, which is why the scan stays as a maybe.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): If the MRI happens, is it with dye? I am frightened of closed machines also. Sorry, that is a tangent, my cousin hated hers.

[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): If we do it, it would be a plain MRI head, no contrast from my side. We are not arranging it today, only if you are not better in two weeks. The closed space we can talk about then.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): And you definitely think it is the migraine, not the pressure thing?

[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think migraine is the leading idea, provisional, not proven. Raised pressure is the thing I have not excluded. I am not going to pretend the tests have answered it. There is no test result in front of me.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I will do the diary, continue the tablets the way you said, and I will come in two weeks. If I am worse before that I will go to emergency. Thank you, doctor.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Current paracetamol most days supported; 1 g dose is uncertain, not confirmed.
bad.text: Paracetamol (generic_name=paracetamol, dose=1 g, frequency=most days, indication=headache, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient reported the headache can sometimes involve the whole head, although the left side is worse.
On bad mornings the headache is severe enough that she cannot do the school run and has to lie down until it eases.
The headache somewhat eases as the day goes on and by afternoon is dull rather than the morning-type pain.
With her old migraines she would feel sick but rarely vomited; the morning vomiting is new compared with prior migraine attacks.
Photophobia was not established: patient gave an equivocal answer and then said to ignore it, and doctor said he would not rely on light sensitivity as a symptom.

Snoring was specifically not confirmed: husband had reported loud snoring, but patient only gave a hedged answer and doctor stated he would not record snoring as a definite finding; there was explicit disagreement between husband’s report and the patient.
Patient denied taking any other tablets and said she had not started anything else.
Doctor stated he is not starting a new medicine today.
Doctor stated he is not booking the MRI today.

Doctor’s safety-netting included trouble seeing as an emergency symptom; recorded facts say 'trouble seeing' but the transcript also separately included sudden much worse headache, new weakness, and confusion as same-day emergency triggers.
Doctor said he was not hearing a heart complaint that needs chasing today in response to the patient feeling anxious and feeling her heart.
Patient noted light was a bit uncomfortable during the exam, but doctor said that discomfort was not a sign he was using.
Doctor documented that optic discs looked normal on ophthalmoscopy and that a normal quick neurological examination does not by itself exclude a pressure problem.
If MRI is needed, doctor specified it would be a plain MRI head with no contrast ('no dye') from his side.
Doctor explicitly said migraine is the leading idea only provisionally and not proven, and that there is no test result in front of him.
